en.title: Why Hong Kong banks have shut down 40% of branches in recent years
en.summary: Hong Kong bank branches have declined by 40 percent to approximately 900 from 1,500 in recent years as customers increasingly conduct banking transactions online and at non-traditional hours.

en.title: Asia-Pacific hotels a 'most compelling' investment amid travel growth, flat supply: CBRE
en.summary: Asia-Pacific hotel investments reached 8 billion dollars in the first half of the year, up 21 percent annually, driven by increased consumer travel demand and limited supply of new properties.

stories.title: Mooncakes for the dog? How China is reinventing its iconic festive snack

en.title: Mooncakes for the dog? How China is reinventing its iconic festive snack
en.summary: Pet mooncakes have become a popular product in China during the Mid-Autumn Festival season, with specialized versions for dogs and cats appearing in major retailers and online stores. Products are selling quickly, with some packs priced around 50 yuan generating thousands of sales.

en.title: Morgan Stanley deal leak triggers rival poaching, security warnings for Hong Kong banks
en.summary: Following an accidental disclosure of confidential deal information by Morgan Stanley, competing investment banks in Hong Kong are actively approaching affected clients to solicit their business, capitalizing on the security breach.
